cross_product_finding: This page is the clearest evidence in the batch that Capella's access-control surface is a genuinely different shape from server/'s RBAC privilege model, and does NOT map cleanly onto requiresPrivilege. What this page describes instead is a layered model: (1) identity/authentication - federated SSO with named IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Ping Identity, CyberArk) plus MFA with account lockout after 5 failed attempts; (2) authorization - organization- and project-scoped 'user roles' (not a flat privilege list like privilege:query-manage-index); (3) network-boundary controls - Allowed IPs, VPC peering, private endpoints, and a limited-availability 'restrict public access' toggle, which are access-control mechanisms that have no server/ RBAC equivalent at all; (4) secrets/credential lifecycle - a Hashicorp Vault plugin issuing dynamic, short-lived cluster credentials, and a separate 'Cluster Credentials' concept for programmatic/application access. None of these primitives is a discrete, nameable 'privilege' the way privilege:query-manage-index is on server/. I minted requiresOrganizationRole as the closest analog to requiresPrivilege, but flag that it is coarser-grained (role assigned at org/project level) rather than action-level (privilege granted for a specific operation like manage-index). The coordinator should treat security:access-management/org:organization-project-role-model as a parallel, not a substitute, vocabulary to privilege:query-manage-index - the two are unlikely to ever need cross-links, since Capella clusters still run Couchbase Server underneath and may still expose per-database RBAC privileges at a lower layer (e.g. via cluster credentials/SDK auth) that simply aren't surfaced on this particular overview page.
